title: the Ninefold Court Rising Again
premise: Quentin Lockridge has spent his whole life in Hollowmere, a valley where the old magic of the Ninefold Court cannot reach, hiding his gift for speaking with beasts. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and his secret is betrayed by someone he loves, he flees into a country that was erased from maps a century ago, guided by animals who remember what humans chose to forget. To survive, he must find the Thirteenth Door—the last way out of the dead kingdom—before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, while learning that the inheritance he carries is not just a curse but a claim to the vanished court itself. In the end, Quentin opens the door not to escape but to let the Ninefold Court rise again through him, choosing truth over the safety of silence.
about_author: Jude Almeida is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to things that could not speak back in words. They write fantasy about quiet people carrying loud secrets.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. In Hollowmere, where magic dies at the ridge line, Quentin quietly heals a wounded fox with words no one must hear him speak. His grandmother warns that gifts like his are why their family came here generations ago. Emotional beat: tender secrecy—the comfort and suffocation of a life built on hiding.

chapters.title: A Proclamation on the Church Door
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The crown posts a decree: all beast-speakers are traitors to be hunted, and informants will be paid in land. Quentin watches neighbors read it hungrily, realizing invisibility was always an illusion. Emotional beat: dread blooming into resolve as he begins planning an escape he doesn't know how to make.

chapters.title: The Fox Who Remembers Roads
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A dying old vixen tells Quentin of the Thirteenth Door beyond the valley, in the country erased from every map after the Ninefold Court fell. She gives him a debt: carry her memory north. Emotional beat: wonder and grief intertwined—a quest offered by a creature with hours left to live.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: POV Wren, Quentin's closest friend. Wren sees Quentin speaking to crows and, terrified and tempted by the reward, reports him—or believes she did. Her chapter reveals her own buried family history with the Court. Emotional beat: guilt curdling; loyalty tested against survival before any betrayal occurs.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Witch-hunters arrive at dawn, led by an informant whose voice Quentin recognizes as Wren's. He escapes through the marshes with the help of every animal he's ever helped, crossing the ridge where magic can finally touch him—and nearly kills him. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpened into flight; grief he cannot afford to feel yet.

chapters.title: The Country With No Name
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Beyond the border lies the erased kingdom: ruined courts, roads that move, beasts who remember being courtiers. A stag-herald tests Quentin's gift and names him heir-blood of the Ninth Seat. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by fear—he is not fleeing his inheritance; he is walking into it.

chapters.title: The Hunt Behind the Moon
chapters.summary: POV alternating Quentin and Wren. The crown's chief hunter enters the dead country too, armed with a relic that silences beast-speech. Wren, wracked by what she did, follows to undo her betrayal. Emotional beat: pursuit tightening; two converging journeys toward the same door.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ninth Seat
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. At the door's threshold, the Court's remnant demands its price: the heir must give up the valley-life, the name Lockridge, and the possibility of ever returning to safety. Quentin learns Wren followed him and refuses to believe she meant harm. Emotional beat: the cost made explicit—inheritance as sacrifice, not prize.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Quentin and Wren. On the final night, the hunter corners them at the Door; Wren takes the relic's blow meant for Quentin, and her act breaks the relic's power—truth spoken aloud unseals what silence sealed. Quentin claims the Ninth Seat and opens the Door. Emotional beat: climax—loyalty redeemed by truth at the moment of greatest danger.

chapters.title: The Court Rising
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The Ninefold Court rises again—not as conquest but as covenant between human and beast, with Quentin as its speaker and Wren, forgiven, as its first sworn witness. The valley below will change whether it likes it or not. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—an ending that is also a beginning, and a home left behind forever.
